title_en: Peng Yuxiang v. Nanjing Urban Construction Development (Group) Co., Ltd. — dispute over recovery of labor remuneration
ruling_gist_en: Where an employer stipulates that an employee may receive a bonus after completing certain performance targets, but without justifiable reason refuses to fulfill the relevant approval obligations, and the employee claims that the conditions for receiving the bonus are satisfied and requests the employer to issue the bonus in accordance with the regulations, the people's court shall support such claim.
keywords_en: civil; dispute over recovery of labor remuneration; second instance; intermediate people's court; Jiangsu Province; natural person; legal person; Labor Law; Labor Contract Law; whether conditions for bonus payment are satisfied; fulfillment of approval obligations; validity of internal reward distribution plan; reversal of judgment; introduction of investment projects; bonus application and approval; distribution as per meeting minutes; good faith; dispute over recovery of labor remuneration from a limited liability company
full_text_en:
Peng Yuxiang v. Nanjing Urban Construction and Development (Group) Co., Ltd. — dispute over recovery of labor remuneration

[Ruling Summary]

Where an employer stipulates that an employee may obtain a bonus after achieving certain performance targets, but the employer, without legitimate justification, refuses to perform the relevant approval obligations, and the employee claims that the conditions for receiving the bonus have been satisfied and requests the employer to grant the bonus in accordance with the rules, the People's Court shall support such claim.

Plaintiff: Peng Yuxiang, male, born January 20, 1986, Han nationality, residing in Gulou District, Nanjing, Jiangsu Province.

Defendant: Nanjing Urban Construction and Development (Group) Co., Ltd., domiciled at Hongwu Road, Qinhuai District, Nanjing, Jiangsu Province.

Legal Representative: Yao Xiaogang, General Manager of the company.

The plaintiff, Peng Yuxiang, filed a lawsuit with the Qinhuai District People's Court of Nanjing, Jiangsu Province, against the defendant, Nanjing Urban Construction and Development (Group) Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Chengkai Company), concerning a dispute over recovery of labor remuneration.

Plaintiff's Allegations: The defendant, Chengkai Company, formulated the "Interim Measures of Nanjing Chengkai Group on Rewards for Introducing Investment Projects" (Ning Kaicheng Fa Wen [2016] No. 89, hereinafter referred to as Document No. 89) on August 12, 2016, which stipulated that rewards would be given to personnel and teams that introduced projects to the company. Peng Yuxiang joined the company on February 27, 2017, as the head of the Investment and Development Department and was responsible for introducing real estate investment projects. On June 12, 2017, the Investment and Development Department where Peng Yuxiang worked passed an internal "Meeting Minutes" determining that Peng Yuxiang was entitled to 75% of the team reward of the Investment and Development Department. Subsequently, during his tenure, Peng Yuxiang led the Investment and Development Department in successfully securing six projects for Chengkai Company: Wuxi Hongmei Xintiandi, Yangzhou GZ051 Plot, Rugao York Town (hereinafter collectively referred to as the Wuxi and other three projects), Xuzhou Jiaozhuang, Gaoyou Hongji Wanhecheng, and Xuzhou Pengcheng Machinery (hereinafter collectively referred to as the Xuzhou and other three projects). The Investment and Development Department submitted six reward applications to Chengkai Company in accordance with Document No. 89. Among them, the reward applications for the Wuxi and other three projects had been approved but Chengkai Company refused to fulfill them, while for the Xuzhou and other three projects, Chengkai Company refused to approve them. Based on Document No. 89 and the "Meeting Minutes" of the Investment and Development Department, Peng Yuxiang now requests Chengkai Company to pay him a reward of RMB 1,689,083.

Defendant's Defense: 1. The plaintiff, Peng Yuxiang, had dereliction of duty by concealing key information in the Wuxi Hongmei Xintiandi project and the Rugao York Town project, causing significant losses to Chengkai Company, and therefore should not receive any reward. 2. Even if Peng Yuxiang did successfully introduce the six projects to Chengkai Company and prima facie satisfied the conditions for receiving the reward under Document No. 89, because although the reward applications for the Wuxi and other three projects were signed for approval by Yao Xiaogang, the legal representative of Chengkai Company, the main text of the reward applications did not specify the proportion of reward distribution among departments and personnel, and the reward applications for the Xuzhou and other three projects had not undergone any approval process, the approval procedures for the six projects were therefore incomplete, and the corresponding rewards should not be distributed. 3. The "Meeting Minutes" were not signed by all personnel of the Investment and Development Department, nor were they approved or filed with the company. Peng Yuxiang is not entitled to 75% of the team reward of the Investment and Development Department based on that document.

First Instance – Facts Found by the Court:

The defendant, Chengkai Company, issued Document No. 89 on August 12, 2016, stipulating that for the successful introduction of commercial housing projects, Chengkai Company would determine the total reward amount based on the expected project profit or return approved by the board of directors of Greenland Holding Group Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Greenland Group), taking into comprehensive consideration factors such as project scale, annualized average profit margin, and consolidated statements, and setting the total reward at 0.1% to 0.5%. The reward was to be applied for by the Investment and Development Department after formulating the specific reward composition for each department or other personnel, and distributed after review and approval by the group's leadership.

On February 27, 2017, the plaintiff, Peng Yuxiang, joined the defendant, Chengkai Company, as the manager of the Investment and Development Department. On June 12, 2017, four persons from the Investment and Development Department — Peng Yuxiang, Feng, Guan, and Jiang — held a discussion meeting and formed "Meeting Minutes," determining that the internal distribution plan for the reward within the department was: the general manager (i.e., Peng Yuxiang) would receive 75% of the total bonus amount, and project participants would receive 25%.

During the plaintiff Peng Yuxiang's tenure, the Investment and Development Department under his leadership successfully secured six projects: Wuxi Hongmei Xintiandi, Yangzhou GZ051 Plot, Rugao York Town, Xuzhou Jiaozhuang, Gaoyou Hongji Wanhecheng, and Xuzhou Pengcheng Machinery. Subsequently, the Investment and Development Department submitted six reward applications to the defendant, Chengkai Company, regarding the aforementioned six projects. Among them: 1. The reward applications for the Wuxi and other three projects stated that, based on the project profits (RMB 154.32 million, RMB 68.17 million, and RMB 143.65 million respectively), it was recommended to grant rewards at rates of 0.4%, 0.5%, and 0.4%, with total reward amounts of RMB 617,300, RMB 340,000, and RMB 574,400 respectively. The lower part of the main text of the applications bore the signatures of Fa, Director of the Planning and Operations Department of Chengkai Company; Zhu, Director and Party Committee Secretary; and Yao Xiaogang, Legal Representative, indicating approval. Attached after the main text of the applications were bonus distribution tables with no signatures or seals, showing the composition of reward distribution among departments and other personnel, with the reward amounts for the Investment and Development Department being RMB 502,300, RMB 200,000, and RMB 454,400 respectively. 2. The reward applications for the Xuzhou and other three projects stated that, based on the project profits (RMB 192.05 million, RMB 148.10 million, and RMB 110.47 million respectively), it was recommended to grant rewards at rates of 0.4%, 0.2%, and 0.3%, with total reward amounts of RMB 768,200, RMB 296,200, and RMB 341,410 respectively. An appendix table at the end of the main text of the applications indicated the composition of reward distribution among departments and other personnel, with the reward amounts for the Investment and Development Department being RMB 568,000, RMB 226,000, and RMB 301,410 respectively. The reward applications for the Xuzhou and other three projects did not bear the signature of the legal representative of Chengkai Company nor the company seal of Chengkai Company.

Subsequently, because the defendant, Chengkai Company, did not pay the aforementioned rewards to the plaintiff, Peng Yuxiang, on June 5, 2018, Peng Yuxiang filed an arbitration application with the Nanjing Qinhuai District Labor and Personnel Dispute Arbitration Committee, requesting that Chengkai Company pay him a total reward of RMB 1,689,083. On June 13 of the same year, the committee issued an "Acceptance Confirmation Letter," and Peng Yuxiang then filed a lawsuit with the Qinhuai District People's Court of Nanjing, Jiangsu Province, within the statutory period.

During the first instance trial, the defendant, Chengkai Company, challenged the validity of the "Meeting Minutes" on the ground that the number of personnel in the Investment and Development Department during Peng Yuxiang's tenure as its head was more than four. The first instance court therefore requested both parties to provide a list of members of the Investment and Development Department during Peng Yuxiang's term. Chengkai Company submitted a "List of Department Members," but due to obvious inconsistencies in the list, the court admonished it in court. Thereafter, Chengkai Company did not submit further evidence. Meanwhile, Peng Yuxiang also did not submit corresponding evidence to the first instance court regarding the composition of the Investment and Development Department.

First Instance – Opinion of the Qinhuai District People's Court of Nanjing, Jiangsu Province:

Taking the signature for approval of the defendant Chengkai Company's legal representative, Yao Xiaogang, as the criterion, the six projects involved in this case can be divided into two categories: one being the Wuxi and other three projects, and the other being the Xuzhou and other three projects.

For the Wuxi and other three projects, the Investment and Development Department submitted a written application to the defendant, Chengkai Company, and the application was signed for approval by Yao Xiaogang, the legal representative of Chengkai Company. Although Chengkai Company claimed that the reward required approval by the board of directors before implementation, it did not submit evidence to prove that any further procedures were required beyond the signature and approval of the legal representative, nor did it submit evidence that the three signed and approved reward applications had been revoked. Therefore, the approval procedures for these three project reward applications were completed, and Chengkai Company should distribute the rewards to the Investment and Development Department accordingly. However, the bonus distribution tables attached to the three project reward applications, which contained the specific reward amounts due to the Investment and Development Department, bore no signatures or seals of Chengkai Company. Thus, the specific share of the reward due to the Investment and Development Department could not be determined. The "Meeting Minutes," which concerned the distribution of bonuses among all members of the Investment and Development Department, bore only the signatures of the four persons: plaintiff Peng Yuxiang, Feng, Guan, and Jiang. Peng Yuxiang did not provide evidence that other personnel in the department voluntarily waived their right to participate in the departmental reward distribution or acknowledged the minutes. Therefore, there was insufficient basis for his claim to 75% of the reward of the Investment and Development Department. Accordingly, the claim regarding the Wuxi and other three projects was not supported.

For the Xuzhou and other three projects, the plaintiff, Peng Yuxiang, did not provide evidence confirming that he had submitted reward applications to Chengkai Company. The three projects had not completed the approval procedures. Therefore, the claim regarding the Xuzhou and other three projects was not supported.

Accordingly, the Qinhuai District People's Court of Nanjing, Jiangsu Province, based on Article 47 of the Labor Law of the People's Republic of China, Article 18 of the Labor Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, and Article 64 and Article 142 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, rendered the following judgment on September 11, 2018:

Reject all of Peng Yuxiang's claims.

Peng Yuxiang refused to accept the judgment and appealed to the Nanjing Intermediate People's Court of Jiangsu Province: (1) The bonus distribution tables attached to the reward applications for the Wuxi and other three projects were actually submitted together with the reward applications to Yao Xiaogang and others for approval. Although they were not independently signed, their authenticity could still be confirmed by reference to the following evidence: a. Document No. 89 clearly stipulates that "after obtaining a project, the Group Investment and Development Department shall submit a written application, including the list of rewarded persons or teams, the method and standard of reward, etc." Therefore, the reward application prepared by the Investment and Development Department must have included the bonus distribution table, and it would have been impossible for the group leaders to sign the reward application without a list. b. The proportion of the Investment and Development Department's reward in the bonus distribution table can be cross-verified with the following evidence to prove its authenticity: On August 3, 2017, the "Greenland Holding Group Investment Line Incentive Measures (Discussion Draft)" and the WeChat chat records between Peng Yuxiang and the appellee Chengkai Company's legal representative Yao Xiaogang, Director of Planning and Operations Department Fa, and Wang, an employee of Greenland Group, Chengkai Company's controlling shareholder, demonstrated that Greenland Group had issued a document clearly stating that the reward share for the investment line was 70%-80%, and for other supporting lines, 20%-30%. The "Report on Project Development Rewards" issued on January 13, 2017, by Yangzhou Shengcheng Real Estate Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Yangzhou Company), a subsidiary of Chengkai Company, proved that Yangzhou Company, which held a position equivalent to the Investment and Development Department, received 72% of the total bonus after obtaining the Tianshunxi Project. Conversely, Chengkai Company now acknowledges that the main text of the reward applications has been approved, but only challenges the attached bonus distribution tables. It should bear the burden of proving that these tables were not approved. (2) The approval procedures for the reward applications for the Xuzhou and other three projects were indeed not completed, but this was because Chengkai Company deliberately refused to approve them. The court should focus on whether Peng Yuxiang substantially completed the projects in question and whether his application fell within the reward scope of Document No. 89, rather than being limited to whether the approval procedures were completed. (3) At the time the "Meeting Minutes" were formed, the personnel in the investment line of the Investment and Development Department were only four persons: Peng Yuxiang, Jiang, Feng, and Guan. All of them participated in the "Meeting Minutes" and agreed to the distribution ratio. The first instance court's requirement that Peng Yuxiang should prove, person by person, that other personnel who could not participate in the bonus distribution agreed to the ratio exceeded reasonable limits. The "Meeting Minutes" were indeed not filed with the company, but Chengkai Company did not require that departmental bonus distribution plans be filed.

Appellee Chengkai Company's Defense: (1) Whether to distribute rewards and how to distribute them are part of Chengkai Company's operational management rights. As the employer and the entity responsible for distributing bonuses, Chengkai Company has the right to decide independently. Although the reward applications for the Wuxi and other three projects were approved by the relevant departments of Chengkai Company, the approval was only for the total bonus amount. The bonus distribution tables attached to the three reward application forms were unilaterally submitted by the appellant Peng Yuxiang and were not approved or acknowledged by Chengkai Company, and thus cannot serve as the basis for Peng Yuxiang's claim for reward. For the Xuzhou and other three projects, Chengkai Company did not approve any reward at all, so Peng Yuxiang's claim for land acquisition rewards for these three projects has no basis. (2) During his work, Peng Yuxiang engaged in dereliction of duty, falsification, and concealment of key project information, causing losses of over RMB 30 million to Chengkai Company. Chengkai Company should not pay any reward to Peng Yuxiang. (3) The "Meeting Minutes" involves the significant personal interests of employees and is essentially part of the company's compensation distribution system. Peng Yuxiang had no authority to formulate the relevant distribution plan without authorization from the company. Moreover, the "Meeting Minutes" were not formulated with the participation of all employees of the Investment and Development Department and therefore have no legal effect. Peng Yuxiang is not entitled, based on these minutes, to claim 75% of the bonus of the Investment and Development Department. The first instance judgment found clear facts and correctly applied the law. The appellee requests that the appeal be dismissed and the original judgment be affirmed.

Second Instance – Facts Found by the Nanjing Intermediate People's Court of Jiangsu Province:

On June 12, 2018, the appellant Peng Yuxiang applied for labor arbitration to the Nanjing Qinhuai District Labor and Personnel Dispute Arbitration Committee, requesting to terminate the labor relationship with the appellee Chengkai Company and to be paid corresponding compensation, citing unpaid labor remuneration. According to Articles 36, 37, and 38 of the Labor Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, when an employee actively terminates the labor relationship with the employer, the labor relationship between the parties shall be terminated no later than thirty days thereafter. Therefore, after July 12, 2018, there was no longer a labor relationship between Peng Yuxiang and Chengkai Company.

During the second instance trial, the court inquired of the appellee, Chengkai Company, regarding the scope of "principal leaders of the group" authorized to approve under Document No. 89, the specific approval standards and methods, and the method for determining the proportion of reward distribution among rewarded persons. Chengkai Company submitted a "Statement of Circumstances" clarifying that the "principal leaders of the group" authorized to approve under the approval procedures of Document No. 89 were three persons: Yao Xiaogang, Legal Representative of Chengkai Company; Zhu, Director and Party Committee Secretary; and Fa, Director of the Planning and Operations Department. For the remaining questions, Chengkai Company replied that there were no specific provisions and no supporting rules and regulations to clarify them. The court asked if the appellant Peng Yuxiang were to continue to apply for the bonus distribution ratio for the Wuxi and other three projects or for the rewards of the Xuzhou and other three projects at the current stage, whether Chengkai Company would initiate the review procedure. Chengkai Company replied that since Peng Yuxiang had already left the company, it should be considered that he had waived any potential reward he might have received, and therefore no further review would be conducted. However, Chengkai Company simultaneously admitted that there was no internal company regulation providing that departing employees should not receive corresponding rewards. Additionally, because Chengkai Company claimed that the bonus belonging to the Investment and Development Department should not be distributed solely among the four persons who signed the "Meeting Minutes," the court requested Chengkai Company to clarify which employees were entitled to receive the rewards for the Wuxi and other three projects for which the total reward amount had already been approved. Chengkai Company refused to provide a direct answer, stating that the company had decided not to distribute the rewards.

Second Instance – Opinion of the Nanjing Intermediate People's Court of Jiangsu Province:

The focus of the dispute in this case is whether the appellee, Chengkai Company, should pay the appellant, Peng Yuxiang, the rewards for the six projects including Wuxi Hongmei Xintiandi, and if so, how the corresponding amount should be determined. Specifically, this can be elaborated as: 1. Whether Chengkai Company should distribute rewards to the Investment and Development Department for the six projects involved in this case, including Wuxi Hongmei Xintiandi, in accordance with Document No. 89; 2. If Chengkai Company should distribute the corresponding rewards, how the amount of the reward that the Investment and Development Department (as one of the reward recipients) is entitled to should be determined, i.e., how to determine the proportion of the Investment and Development Department in the total reward; 3. Whether the head of the Investment and Development Department, Peng Yuxiang, can obtain 75% of the reward of the Investment and Development Department based on the "Meeting Minutes."

I. Whether the Appellee, Chengkai Company, Should Distribute Rewards to the Investment and Development Department for the Six Projects Including Wuxi Hongmei Xintiandi in Accordance with Document No. 89.

First, based on Document No. 89 and the "Statement of Circumstances," the following facts can be confirmed: (1) The reward condition under Document No. 89 is that the appellee, Chengkai Company, introduced investment projects that conform to the Group's strategic development goals; (2) The reward objects under Document No. 89 are employees or teams of the Group who provided project information for the introduction of investment projects and made contributions to the ultimate introduction of the project; (3) The reward standard under Document No. 89 is the expected project profit or return of the introduced project multiplied by a coefficient (0.1% - 0.5%); (4) The application process under Document No. 89 is that the Investment and Development Department submits a written reward application including the list of rewarded persons or teams, the method and standard of reward, for approval by Fa, Director of the Planning and Operations Department of Chengkai Company; Zhu, Deputy General Manager; and Yao Xiaogang, General Manager. Among these provisions, the reward objects define the scope of persons targeted by the reward in question; the reward conditions define the elements required to obtain the reward in question; the reward standard defines the method for determining the amount of the reward in question; and the application process defines the review process that the recipient must undergo to realize the reward rights. Among them, the application process and the reward standard do not contain substantive evaluation elements regarding whether the applicant meets the reward conditions. Therefore, the reward application submitted by the Investment and Development Department where the appellant Peng Yuxiang worked should be examined from the perspectives of both the reward objects and the reward conditions. In terms of the reward objects set out in Document No. 89, the Investment and Development Department has the primary responsibility of introducing projects and plays a leading role in Chengkai Company's introduction of various projects. Therefore, it is a qualified reward recipient under the document. In terms of the reward conditions set out in Document No. 89, the Investment and Development Department has successfully introduced for Chengkai Company six projects that conform to Chengkai Company's strategic development goals: Wuxi Hongmei Xintiandi, Yangzhou GZ051 Plot, Rugao York Town, Xuzhou Jiaozhuang, Gaoyou Hongji Wanhecheng, and Xuzhou Pengcheng Machinery, thereby meeting the reward conditions stipulated in the document. Therefore, with respect to the six projects in question, the Investment and Development Department where Peng Yuxiang worked has, on its face, satisfied the conditions for applying for rewards under Document No. 89. If Chengkai Company disagrees with the distribution of the corresponding rewards, in accordance with Article 2, Paragraph 3 of the "Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Evidence in Civil Proceedings," which states that "the parties have the responsibility to provide evidence to prove the facts on which their claims are based or the facts on which they rebut the other party's claims," it shall provide reasons and submit evidence to prove them.

Part 2/2

The appellee, Chengkai Company, argued that the Wuxi Hongmei Xintiandi Project and the Rugao Yuke Town Project introduced by the appellant, Peng Yuxiang, incurred significant losses, and that Peng Yuxiang personally committed serious dereliction of duty in these two projects. Therefore, he did not substantively meet the conditions for receiving the reward. The court held that, as of the conclusion of the case, Chengkai Company had not submitted evidence to prove that the two projects failed to achieve expected profits or would inevitably incur losses. Moreover, even if the two projects did incur losses, since Document No. 89 uses the "expected profit of the introduced project" as the calculation basis for the reward amount, which reflects that the assessment standard is the individual project rather than all projects, this factor should only be considered in determining whether Chengkai Company should issue rewards for the relevant two projects. Chengkai Company's argument that rewards for all six projects should not be paid due to losses on two projects lacked a corresponding basis. More importantly, the condition for receiving the reward under Document No. 89 is merely the introduction of a project; it does not stipulate that project profitability is a prerequisite for the reward. That is, Document No. 89 itself does not make the profitability of a relevant project a condition for determining whether a recipient qualifies for the reward. Therefore, Chengkai Company's defense that rewards should not be paid because the projects incurred losses was untenable. Similarly, Chengkai Company's claim that Peng Yuxiang concealed key facts in the Wuxi Hongmei Xintiandi and Rugao Yoke Town projects, constituting serious dereliction of duty, could not be established as it failed to submit sufficient evidence to prove it. Consequently, the court did not accept Chengkai Company's argument that the Investment and Development Department, where Peng Yuxiang worked, substantially did not meet the conditions for obtaining rewards under Document No. 89.

Secondly, the fact that the reward applications for the six projects involved in the case had not undergone review or the approval process had not been completed could not serve as a reason for the appellee, Chengkai Company, to refuse to pay the project bonus to the appellant, Peng Yuxiang. As the entity establishing the bonus, the employer has the right to set corresponding assessment standards, review criteria, or approval procedures. From the employee's perspective, a potential recipient, after a preliminary self-assessment that the conditions for the reward have been met, must follow the steps stipulated in the approval process to realize the reward. From the employer's perspective, the employer relies on the approval process, applying the eligibility criteria, conditions for the reward, and corresponding reward standards pre-established in the assessment standards, to evaluate whether the employee meets the conditions for the reward, the magnitude of the employee's contribution, and the specific reward amount. Therefore, the assessment standards are the substantive evaluation factors for determining whether an employee qualifies for the reward, while the assessment process constitutes procedural steps for the employer to exercise its assessment power. Unless otherwise expressly provided (e.g., a clear stipulation that failure to claim within a specified period is deemed a waiver of the corresponding right), since the process itself does not involve reward evaluation criteria, whether the approval process has been completed cannot become a substantive evaluation element for whether an employee can receive the bonus. The employer should not attempt to obstruct the realization of the employee's substantive right to receive the bonus on the grounds that the procedural approval process has not been completed. If employers were allowed to use the lack of approval as a reason not to pay bonuses, then an employer's failure to process an employee's bonus application, or even maliciously failing to initiate or complete the relevant procedures, would render it nearly impossible for employees to realize their right to the pre-established reward. In this case, Document No. 89 did not set a time limit for applying for the reward, nor did it stipulate that an applicant who resigned would forfeit the right to claim the corresponding reward. Therefore, Chengkai Company's argument that Peng Yuxiang's right to receive the corresponding reward should be denied because the approval process for the six projects had not been initiated or completed was untenable.

Furthermore, conducting a substantive review of an employee's reward application is not only the employer's right but also its obligation. The appellee, Chengkai Company, argued that the right to approve the disbursement of rewards was part of the company's employment autonomy, and it had the right to decide whether to approve, pay, or withhold rewards and how to pay them. The court held that, in this case, Document No. 89 states: "In order to effectively stimulate the enthusiasm of employees and teams within the group, encourage employees to work creatively, and incentivize employees and teams who make special contributions during the group's project acquisition process, these measures are hereby formulated," and "The reward methods include... cash rewards." Article 4 of the *Regulations on the Composition of Total Wages* of the National Bureau of Statistics stipulates that total wages consist of the following six components: (1) time wages; (2) piecework wages; (3) bonuses; (4) allowances and subsidies; (5) overtime wages; and (6) wages paid under special circumstances. Article 7 stipulates that bonuses refer to labor remuneration paid to employees for above-quota labor and for increasing revenue and saving expenses. This includes (1) production bonuses; (2) savings bonuses; (3) labor competition bonuses; (4) incentive wages for government agencies and institutions; (5) other bonuses. It can be seen that the cash rewards established by Document No. 89 constitute above-quota labor remuneration promised by Chengkai Company to employees to encourage creative work. In nature, this falls under "other bonuses" as defined in the *Regulations on the Composition of Total Wages*. Under these circumstances, Document No. 89 should not merely be regarded as a unilateral incentive act by Chengkai Company towards its employees based on its employment autonomy, but also as an agreement formed between Chengkai Company and unspecified employees, including the appellant, Peng Yuxiang, regarding the acquisition of this reward. That is, on the basis of the employees' existing compensation, Chengkai Company promised additional labor remuneration to stimulate their work enthusiasm, prompting employees to fully leverage their initiative to create more value for the company. It also committed that when employees make corresponding efforts and achieve the performance stipulated in Document No. 89, the company would provide them with this additional remunerative reward beyond their existing salary. In this case, if Peng Yuxiang, through his efforts, met the conditions for receiving the reward set out in Document No. 89, and he submitted an application to Chengkai Company requesting the realization of this above-quota labor remuneration, whether based on the principle of good faith or the principle of distribution according to work, Chengkai Company was obligated to initiate the review process to examine the reward application and determine whether Peng Yuxiang's right to the bonus could materialize.

As for the appellee Chengkai Company's argument that the appellant Peng Yuxiang had already resigned, and therefore he should be deemed to have voluntarily waived his rights to the reward, this argument also could not stand. Document No. 89 does not stipulate that an employee's voluntary resignation constitutes a waiver of related rewards under it. Furthermore, there was no evidence to suggest that Peng Yuxiang voluntarily waived his right to receive the bonuses in question. Hence, this appellate argument by Chengkai Company was not accepted.

In summary, given that the Investment and Development Department, where the appellant Peng Yuxiang worked, had successfully acquired the land and met the conditions for receiving the reward, the appellee, Chengkai Company, was obligated to review Peng Yuxiang's application. If Chengkai Company refused to review it, it was required to provide a reasonable justification. In this case, Chengkai Company's claims regarding Peng Yuxiang's dereliction of duty and the losses incurred by the projects in question were untenable due to a lack of factual basis. Chengkai Company also failed to provide a reasonable explanation for its refusal to review. Its refusal to fulfill the obligation of approval had already infringed upon Peng Yuxiang's legitimate rights and interests, for which it should bear the corresponding adverse consequences. The court determined that the conditions for the Investment and Development Department, where Peng Yuxiang worked, to receive the rewards under Document No. 89 were met. Chengkai Company was obligated to disburse the rewards for the six projects involved in the case to the Investment and Development Department.

II. How to Determine the Proportion of the Bonus for the Investment and Development Department within the Rewards for the Six Projects.

Regarding the three projects, including Wuxi, since their reward applications had already been signed and confirmed by legal representative Yao Xiaogang, the total reward amounts for these three projects were determined. As to whether the Investment and Development Department could enjoy the bonus rights based on the bonus distribution table attached to the reward application, considering that Document No. 89 explicitly requires that the reward application by the recipient include the list of reward recipients and the reward standards. Furthermore, given that the appellee, Chengkai Company, has now explicitly refused to continue the approval process for the three projects, including Wuxi, without providing a reasoned justification, it should bear the adverse consequences. Also considering that the allocation ratio proposed by the appellant, Peng Yuxiang, is within a reasonable range, based on a comprehensive analysis of the above circumstances, the court determined that the probability that the reward application for the Investment and Development Department attached a list of relevant departments and personnel was higher than the possibility of a reward application containing only a total reward amount without mentioning any recipient departments, personnel, or recipient proportions. Therefore, the Investment and Development Department should enjoy the corresponding reward share according to the bonus distribution table attached to the reward application.

For the three projects, including Xuzhou, the exact amount of the reward that the Investment and Development Department was entitled to receive could not be directly determined based on the existing evidence in this case. 1. The total reward amount for the three projects, including Xuzhou, could not be determined. The lump-sum reward standard stipulated in Document No. 89 is merely the expected profit or revenue of the introduced project multiplied by a coefficient (0.1%-0.5%). Although the expected profit of each project is a definite figure according to their respective T29 reports, the reward coefficient fluctuates between 0.1% and 0.5%, and there is no specific standard for determining this coefficient. 2. The proportion of the reward attributable to the Investment and Development Department for the three projects, including Xuzhou, could not be directly determined from the reward application form submitted by the appellant, Peng Yuxiang. For the three projects, including Wuxi, the reward application had entered the appellee Chengkai Company's approval process and had received the signed approval of three persons, including Chengkai Company's General Manager Yao Xiaogang. The dispute between the parties was merely whether the content approved at that time included the reward distribution table. Therefore, the court based its determination on the existing materials, focusing on the admissibility of evidence. However, for the three projects, including Xuzhou, because the reward application lacked the approval of Yao Xiaogang and the other two persons, the strength of Peng Yuxiang's evidence supporting his reward claim for these three projects was weaker than that for the three projects, including Wuxi. Peng Yuxiang himself acknowledged this and agreed that the court could exercise its discretion. Based on the basic content of Document No. 89 and the factors that could be determined, the court, guided by the principle of fairness to reasonably balance the interests of both parties, made a discretionary determination:

Regarding the bonus base: According to the T29 project reports for the three projects, including Xuzhou, the expected profits for these three projects were RMB 192.05 million, RMB 148.1 million, and RMB 110.47 million respectively (totaling RMB 450.62 million).

Regarding the reward coefficient: The approved reward coefficients for the three projects, including Wuxi, were 0.4%, 0.5%, and 0.4%. For the three projects, including Xuzhou, the reward coefficients claimed by the appellant Peng Yuxiang himself were 0.4%, 0.2%, and 0.3%. The court exercised its discretion and calculated using 0.2%.

Regarding the reward proportion for the Investment and Development Department: The proportions used in the bonus distribution table for the three projects, including Wuxi, were 81%, 58%, and 79%. For the three projects, including Xuzhou, the proportions claimed by Peng Yuxiang himself were 73.9%, 76%, and 90.8%. The court exercised its discretion and calculated using 58%.

In summary, the amount of bonus payable to the Investment and Development Department for the three projects, including Xuzhou, was RMB 522,700.

III. Whether the Appellee, Peng Yuxiang, is Entitled to Receive 75% of the Investment and Development Department's Bonus Based on the "Meeting Minutes."

Regarding whether the Investment and Development Department had the right to formulate its own reward distribution plan. Article 4 of the *Labor Contract Law of the PRC* stipulates that employing units shall establish and improve rules and regulations in accordance with the law to ensure that workers enjoy labor rights and perform labor obligations. As the formulator of rules and regulations, when an employer issues corresponding reward policies, it is obligated to establish detailed supporting systems to clarify how these reward policies should be specifically implemented. If the employer fails to specify the corresponding implementation rules, and a dispute arises between the employer and employees as a result, the adverse consequences arising from the ambiguity of the system should be borne by the employer, not the employee. Since the appellee, Chengkai Company, had no evidence to prove that it had corresponding regulations stipulating that the right to allocate departmental bonuses belonged to Chengkai Company itself rather than the Investment and Development Department, its assertion that the bonus could only be distributed after discussion by the entire staff representative congress of Chengkai Company lacked effective preconditions. As the recipient of the bonus, the Investment and Development Department should have the right to determine the distribution plan for that bonus.

Regarding whether the "Meeting Minutes" signed by the appellant Peng Yuxiang and three others could be regarded as the expression of intent of the Investment and Development Department. Since the appellee, Chengkai Company, as the entity controlling personnel matters, organizational structure, and rules and regulations, bears the burden of proof regarding the number of personnel in the Investment and Development Department at the time the "Meeting Minutes" were signed. After its initially submitted "Personnel Roster" was refuted by the court of first instance, Chengkai Company failed to submit further evidence to clarify the composition of the Investment and Development Department's personnel, nor could it prove that there were other persons who should have participated in the preparation of the "Meeting Minutes." It should bear the corresponding adverse consequences for this. Accordingly, the court determined that the "Meeting Minutes" should be used as the basis for handling this case, and Peng Yuxiang was entitled to receive 75% of the bonus share of the Investment and Development Department based on it.

In summary, for the three projects, including Wuxi, the appellee, Chengkai Company, shall, in accordance with the reward applications for the three projects and their attached bonus distribution tables, as well as the "Meeting Minutes," pay the appellant, Peng Yuxiang, a reward of RMB 867,525 \[1. Wuxi Hongmei Xintiandi Project: Expected profit RMB 154.32 million × 0.4% (claimed ratio) = RMB 617,300, of which the Investment and Development Department was entitled to RMB 502,300; Peng Yuxiang's individual entitlement was RMB 502,300 × 75% = RMB 376,725. 2. Yangzhou GZ051 Plot Project: Expected profit RMB 68.17 million × 0.5% (claimed ratio) = RMB 340,000, of which the Investment and Development Department was entitled to RMB 200,000; Peng Yuxiang's individual entitlement was RMB 200,000 × 75% = RMB 150,000. 3. Rugao Yoke Town Project: Expected profit RMB 143.65 million × 0.4% (claimed ratio) = RMB 574,400, of which the Investment and Development Department was entitled to RMB 454,400; Peng Yuxiang's individual entitlement was RMB 454,400 × 75% = RMB 340,800\]. For the three projects, including Xuzhou, Chengkai Company shall pay Peng Yuxiang a reward of RMB 392,039.4 (Total expected profit for the three projects: RMB 450.62 million × 0.2% × 58% × 75%). The total of both is RMB 1,259,564.4.

Accordingly, the Nanjing Intermediate People's Court of Jiangsu Province, pursuant to Articles 47 and 87 of the *Labor Contract Law of the PRC*, Article 2 of the *Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Evidence in Civil Proceedings*, and Article 170, Paragraph 1, Item 2 of the *Civil Procedure Law of the PRC*, rendered the following judgment on January 3, 2020:

1. The civil judgment (No. (2018) Su 0104 Min Chu 6032) of the Qinhuai District People's Court of Nanjing was vacated;
2. Nanjing Urban Construction and Development (Group) Co., Ltd. shall pay Peng Yuxiang a bonus of RMB 1,259,564.4 within fifteen days from the date this judgment becomes legally effective.

This judgment is final.
